subject: RFI: Sequestered runtime / operator access for Aurora Health
messages:
From: Elena Marquez <elena.marquez@aurora-health.com>
To: Rohan Mehta <rohan_mehta@redwood.ai>
Cc: Procurement <procurement@aurora-health.com>, SecOps Team <secops@aurora-health.com>
Date: 2027-03-02T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Initial RFI: Sequestered runtime and operator access requirements

Rohan —

Thanks for taking our intake call last week. As we evaluate vendor fit for several clinics, Aurora needs to confirm a few specific capabilities for any private/on-prem deployment (we call this our "Sequestered Runtime" profile). Could you provide concise answers to the items below and attach any specimen docs you have? We need these for our security working group by EOD next Wednesday.

Key asks (please point to attachments where applicable):
- How do you prevent inadvertent egress from an air-gapped or VPC-isolated deployment? We need details on allowed outbound flows and enforcement mechanisms.
- Operator access: can you run the runtime without any external operator authentication (i.e., purely local operator accounts)? If remote operator tooling is used, how is MFA and auditability enforced?
- Offline updates: describe the process for delivering signed runtime updates and model bundles to an air-gapped site. Do you support detached signature verification and package manifests?
- Evidence: sample network segmentation diagram, example operator access matrix, and a short description of your package signing process.

We prefer short bullets and point-form attachments.

Best,
Elena
Elena Marquez
Senior Information Security Manager
Aurora Health

Attachments requested: Network diagram, operator matrix, update process notes

From: Rohan Mehta <rohan_mehta@redwood.ai>
To: Elena Marquez <elena.marquez@aurora-health.com>
Cc: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.ai>, Irene Choi <irene_choi@redwood.ai>
Date: 2027-03-03T11:34:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Initial RFI: Sequestered runtime and operator access requirements

Elena —

Appreciate the clear list. Summary answers below and I attached a short packet (isolation-overview.pdf) with diagrams and a checklist. High-level answers:

1) Preventing egress (short):
- Default-deny egress at OS and network layers: runtime ships with an explicit allowlist for outbound hosts/ports.
- Enforcement: iptables/nftables rules plus a kernel-level process supervisor that asserts socket-level policies.
- Fail-closed: on any policy agent failure the serving nodes drop to a "no-outbound" mode; admin UI is disabled until policy agent is healthy.

2) Operator access (short):
- Support for fully local-only operator accounts (LDAP/AD optional) — operators can be local UIDs with password and key-based login.
- Remote operator tooling: when enabled we require RBAC + MFA + conditional access; every session is logged and session recordings are retained according to customer retention settings.

3) Offline updates (short):
- We provide signed package bundles: runtime binaries, model artifacts, and a canonical manifest.json with SHA256 entries.
- Signatures use customer-owned keys via our recommended workflow (we can sign with customer KMS or provide signed artifacts that the customer verifies with the included public key).
- Verification: an on-site package verifier checks signatures and manifests before install.

Attached files: isolation-overview.pdf (network/ops diagram) and a short checklist.

I'll loop in Irene for deeper operator access specifics and to attach the OperatorAccessMatrix.

Thanks,
Rohan Mehta
Senior Solutions Engineer
Redwood Inference

Attachments referenced: isolation-overview.pdf

From: SecOps Team <secops@aurora-health.com>
To: Rohan Mehta <rohan_mehta@redwood.ai>, Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.ai>, Irene Choi <irene_choi@redwood.ai>
Date: 2027-03-04T08:55:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Initial RFI: Sequestered runtime and operator access requirements

Rohan / team —

Thanks for the packet. A few follow-ups from our security review:
- When you say "fail-closed", what is the expected operator recovery path if the policy agent fails irretrievably? We need documented runbook steps with operator-level commands.
- For local-only operators: can you provide a sample operator onboarding flow (password complexity, account rotation, emergency break-glass)?
- For signed packages: are you able to provide a sample signed manifest and the verifying commandline (we will run this in our test air-gapped lab)?

We also need an OperatorAccessMatrix (CSV or XLSX) that maps roles -> allowed actions (start/stop, deploy, rollbacks, secret access).

Thanks — deadline remains EOD next Wednesday for our summary bundle.

—Aurora SecOps

From: Irene Choi <irene_choi@redwood.ai>
To: SecOps Team <secops@aurora-health.com>, Rohan Mehta <rohan_mehta@redwood.ai>, Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.ai>
Date: 2027-03-05T10:42:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Initial RFI: Sequestered runtime and operator access requirements

Hi Elena / SecOps —

Attached is the OperatorAccessMatrix.xlsx and a short ops note (signed-package-manifest-process.md) showing the exact verification commands. Quick answers inline:

> When you say "fail-closed", what is the expected operator recovery path if the policy agent fails irretrievably?
- Recovery path (short): 1) Identify failing host(s) via out-of-band console; 2) Place node in maintenance (cluster controller marks unschedulable); 3) Use on-site signed bootstrap package to re-provision policy agent; 4) Validate policy integrity via the manifest verifier; 5) Re-enable outbound policy. Full runbook excerpt is in the attached doc.

> For local-only operators: can you provide a sample operator onboarding flow?
- Onboarding steps (short): physical verification of operator identity by customer admin; creation of local account with one-time password; forced public-key enrollment within 72 hours; optional hardware token registration for MFA. Password rotation / account expiry policies are configurable and we recommend 90-day rotation with emergency break-glass using a two-person approval flow.

> For signed packages: sample manifest & commandline
- Example verify: shasum -a 256 -c manifest.sha256 && openssl dgst -sha256 -verify pubkey.pem -signature bundle.sig bundle.tar.gz
- We include a sample manifest (manifest.sha256) and public key with the delivery bundle. See signed-package-manifest-process.md for details.

I've also added a small network diagram (network-segmentation-v2.png) showing recommended VLAN segmentation for operator consoles, control plane, and data plane.

Let us know if your team needs the runbook in a different format or a dry-run session in your air-gapped lab.

Cheers,
Irene Choi
Principal Product Security Engineer
Redwood Inference

Attachments: OperatorAccessMatrix.xlsx, signed-package-manifest-process.md, network-segmentation-v2.png
